items.title: Human Development Index — Concept, Dimensions & Method
items.body:
**In one line:** Human development means widening the real choices people have — to live long, to learn and to enjoy a decent living — and the HDI is the UN's single score that captures it.

**Why it is asked:** The HDI's authors, its three dimensions and how the three are averaged are standard factual questions.

## Idea

- **Human development** = enlarging people's **choices and capabilities**, not just raising income. Philosophical basis: **Amartya Sen's capability approach** (development = expanding real freedoms).
- The **HDI** was created by **Mahbub-ul-Haq** with **Amartya Sen** and launched in the **first Human Development Report (1990)** of the **UNDP**.

## Three dimensions & indicators

| Dimension | Indicator |
|---|---|
| Long & healthy life (health) | Life expectancy at birth |
| Knowledge (education) | Expected years of schooling + Mean years of schooling |
| Decent standard of living (income) | **GNI per capita** in PPP terms (not GDP at market price) |

## Aggregation & categories

- Since HDR 2010 the HDI is the **geometric mean** of the three normalised sub-indices (equal weights).
- Bands: **Low < 0.550 | Medium 0.550-0.699 | High 0.700-0.799 | Very High >= 0.800**.
- Companion indices: **IHDI** (HDI discounted for inequality across the population), **GDI** (female-to-male HDI ratio), **GII** (loss from gender inequality in reproductive health, empowerment, labour market).

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- HDI created by Mahbub-ul-Haq with Amartya Sen; first UNDP Human Development Report in 1990.
- Three dimensions: health (life expectancy), knowledge (expected + mean years of schooling), living standard (GNI per capita PPP).
- HDI is the geometric mean of the three sub-indices (equal weights) since HDR 2010.
- Category bands: Low < 0.550, Medium 0.550-0.699, High 0.700-0.799, Very High >= 0.800.
- Companion measures: IHDI (inequality-adjusted), GDI (female/male HDI ratio), GII (gender inequality).

items.title: India in the Human Development Report 2025
items.body:
**In one line:** The Human Development Report 2025 places India in the 'medium' band at rank 130, up from 134, though inequality still eats into the score.

**Why it is asked:** India's latest rank, its HDI value and the inequality loss are high-value, current-affairs facts.

## Headline

- **HDR 2025** (released **6 May 2025**), themed **"A Matter of Choice: People and Possibilities in the Age of AI"**, ranks **India 130 out of 193** countries with an HDI value of **0.685** — the **Medium Human Development** category, close to the High threshold (0.700).
- India **improved from rank 134 (HDI 0.644)** in the previous HDR 2023-24, driven by gains in **life expectancy** and **GNI per capita**.

## India's component values (HDR 2025)

| Component | Value |
|---|---|
| Life expectancy at birth | ~72.0 years (highest ever) |
| Expected years of schooling | ~13.0 years |
| Mean years of schooling | ~6.2 years |
| GNI per capita (2021 PPP) | ~$9,046 |
| IHDI | ~0.475 (loss ~30.7% to inequality) |
| GDI | ~0.874 |

- Persisting challenges: **income and gender inequality** and **regional gaps** pull down the inequality-adjusted score.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- HDR 2025 (6 May 2025) theme: 'A Matter of Choice: People and Possibilities in the Age of AI'.
- India ranks 130/193 with HDI value 0.685 — Medium Human Development category.
- India rose from rank 134 (HDI 0.644) in HDR 2023-24 to 130 in HDR 2025.
- India's life expectancy ~72 years, expected schooling ~13 years, GNI per capita ~$9,046 (2021 PPP).
- India loses about 30.7% of HDI to inequality (IHDI ~0.475).

items.title: Multidimensional Poverty Index — Global & National
items.body:
**In one line:** The Multidimensional Poverty Index measures poverty as overlapping shortfalls in health, education and living standards, and India runs its own 12-indicator version alongside the global one.

**Why it is asked:** The global-versus-national MPI contrast and India's MPI decline are frequently tested.

## Global MPI

- Published jointly by **UNDP** and the **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)** using the **Alkire-Foster method**.
- **3 dimensions, 10 indicators**. **MPI = H × A** — the product of the headcount ratio and the intensity of poverty — where **H** = share of people who are multidimensionally poor and **A** = average **intensity** (share of weighted deprivations). A person is poor if deprived in **≥ 1/3** of the weighted indicators.

## National MPI (NITI Aayog)

- Retains the **3 dimensions** (Health, Education, Standard of Living) but uses **12 indicators** — the global 10 **plus Maternal Health and Bank Accounts** — aligned to national priorities/schemes.
- **A Progress Review 2023** (based on **NFHS-5, 2019-21**): national headcount fell from **24.85% (2015-16)** to **14.96% (2019-21)**, with about **13.5 crore** people escaping multidimensional poverty. All 12 indicators improved.

| Feature | Global MPI | National MPI |
|---|---|---|
| Dimensions | 3 | 3 |
| Indicators | 10 | 12 |
| Extra indicators | — | Maternal health, Bank accounts |

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- Global MPI: UNDP + OPHI, Alkire-Foster method, 3 dimensions and 10 indicators.
- MPI = H × A (headcount × intensity); poor if deprived in ≥ 1/3 of weighted indicators.
- National MPI (NITI Aayog) has 3 dimensions but 12 indicators — adds maternal health and bank accounts.
- National MPI Progress Review 2023 (NFHS-5): headcount fell 24.85% (2015-16) to 14.96% (2019-21).
- About 13.5 crore people escaped multidimensional poverty between the two NFHS rounds.

items.title: Sustainable Development & the SDGs
items.body:
**In one line:** Sustainable development means meeting today's needs without robbing future generations, and the 17 Sustainable Development Goals are the world's shared 2015-2030 plan to achieve it.

**Why it is asked:** The key reports, their dates and the MDG-to-SDG shift are classic one-mark facts.

## Sustainable development

- **Brundtland Commission**, report **Our Common Future (1987)**: development that **meets present needs without compromising future generations** — the principle of **intergenerational equity**.
- Balances three pillars — **economic, social, environmental** — and highlights a **growth-vs-sustainability trade-off**.
- Alternative welfare measures: the **Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI)**, devised by **Morris David Morris (1979)** from **infant mortality, basic literacy and life expectancy at age 1** (income excluded); **Green GDP** (internalises resource depletion); and Bhutan's **Gross National Happiness**.
- **PAGE (Partnership for Action on Green Economy)** — a UN mechanism supporting greener, inclusive economies — emerged in the context of the **UN Conference on Sustainable Development 2012 (Rio+20), Rio de Janeiro**.
- Milestones: **Stockholm (1972)** -> **Brundtland (1987)** -> **Rio Earth Summit / Agenda 21 (1992)** -> **MDGs (2000-2015)** -> **SDGs (2015-2030)**.

## The SDGs

- The **2030 Agenda** (adopted **September 2015**) sets **17 goals and 169 targets** (monitored via 232 global indicators), succeeding the 8 **Millennium Development Goals**.
- Universal and integrated — no poverty, zero hunger, health, education, gender equality, clean energy, decent work, climate action, etc.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- Sustainable development defined by the Brundtland Report 'Our Common Future' (1987) — intergenerational equity.
- Three pillars: economic, social, environmental; alternatives include Green GDP and Gross National Happiness.
- PQLI (Morris David Morris, 1979) = infant mortality + literacy + life expectancy at age 1 (income excluded).
- PAGE (Partnership for Action on Green Economy) emerged at the UN Conference on Sustainable Development 2012 (Rio+20).
- Milestone sequence: Stockholm 1972 -> Brundtland 1987 -> Rio 1992 -> MDGs 2000 -> SDGs 2015.
- SDGs: 17 goals and 169 targets, adopted September 2015 under the 2030 Agenda.
- SDGs succeeded the 8 Millennium Development Goals (2000-2015).

items.title: SDG India Index & Andhra Pradesh's Performance
items.body:
**In one line:** NITI Aayog's SDG India Index scores every state and union territory on the goals, and Andhra Pradesh ranks as a Front Runner that tops the clean-energy goal.

**Why it is asked:** The index's score bands, its latest toppers and AP's standing are directly examinable.

## SDG India Index (NITI Aayog)

- NITI Aayog's tool to track States/UTs on the SDGs; the **4th edition, SDG India Index 2023-24**, was released in **July 2024** and tracks **16 goals** (SDG 14 excluded from the composite as it is limited to coastal States) on **113 indicators**.
- **Score bands**: Aspirant (0-49), Performer (50-64), **Front Runner (65-99)**, Achiever (100).

## Key 2023-24 results

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| India composite | **71** (up from 66 in 2020-21, 57 in 2018) |
| Top States | **Kerala & Uttarakhand (79)** |
| Lowest State | Bihar (57) |
| Front Runner States/UTs | 32 (up from 22) |

## Andhra Pradesh

- AP is a **Front Runner** State and **topped Goal-7 (Affordable and Clean Energy)** among States — reflecting strong renewable-energy and electrification performance. It serves as a barometer for **Viksit Bharat @2047**.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- SDG India Index is NITI Aayog's State/UT tracker; 4th edition (2023-24) released July 2024.
- Score bands: Aspirant 0-49, Performer 50-64, Front Runner 65-99, Achiever 100.
- India's composite score rose to 71 (from 66 in 2020-21); Kerala and Uttarakhand topped at 79, Bihar lowest at 57.
- 32 States/UTs are now in the Front Runner category (up from 22).
- Andhra Pradesh is a Front Runner and topped Goal-7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) among States.

items.title: HDI — Goalposts, Range, Global Ranks & Related Ideas
items.body:
**In one line:** each HDI dimension is scaled between fixed minimum and maximum "goalposts", the three scores are combined by a geometric mean into a value between 0 and 1, and countries are then ranked.

**Why it is asked:** goalposts, the 0–1 range, the global top and bottom, and the human-capital idea are examined alongside India's rank.

## Goalposts used to scale each dimension (UNDP Technical Notes)

**The story**

| Indicator | Minimum | Maximum |
|---|---|---|
| Life expectancy at birth | **20** years | **85** years |
| Expected years of schooling | 0 | **18** years |
| Mean years of schooling | 0 | **15** years |
| GNI per capita (PPP $) | **$100** | **$75,000** |

- Each **dimension index** = (actual − minimum) ÷ (maximum − minimum); income uses the **natural logarithm** because extra income matters less at high levels.
- The HDI value always lies **between 0 and 1**.

## Global picture in HDR 2025

- **Iceland** ranks **1st** (HDI ≈ 0.972), followed by **Norway** and **Switzerland**; **South Sudan** is last (193rd).
- India is **130th of 193** with **0.685** (Medium band); India's **IHDI** is about **0.475** — a loss of roughly **30.7%** to inequality.

## The indices listed in the source

- **HDI**, **IHDI** (Inequality-adjusted HDI), **GDI** (Gender Development Index) and **AHDI** (**Augmented** HDI — adds a liberal-democracy dimension).

## Related ideas

- **Human capital formation** (education, health, skills) increases people's **knowledge, skill levels and capacities** and builds **intangible** wealth (UPSC 2018).
- Sen's capability approach was set out in his book **"Development as Freedom" (1999)**.
- Across Indian states there is a **positive relationship** between HDI and SDG India Index scores — states that do well on human development also tend to score high on the SDGs.

**TL;DR**
- Goalposts: life expectancy 20–85; expected schooling 18; mean schooling 15; GNI $100–$75,000 (log).
- HDI lies between 0 and 1; geometric mean of three dimension indices.
- HDR 2025: Iceland 1st, South Sudan last; India 130th (0.685).
- Source indices: HDI, IHDI, GDI, AHDI (Augmented HDI).
- Human capital → knowledge, skills, intangible wealth; Sen's "Development as Freedom" (1999).

items.title: The 17 SDGs by Number, the 5 Ps & Global Milestones
items.body:
**In one line:** the 17 Sustainable Development Goals, adopted at the UN on 25 September 2015 and in force from 1 January 2016, are organised around five Ps and grew out of a chain of conferences from Stockholm 1972 to Rio+20.

**Why it is asked:** "Goal number → theme" matching (SDG 7, 13, 14, 16…) and "which conference produced what" are favourite one-liners.

## The 17 goals

**The story**

| No. | Goal | No. | Goal |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | No Poverty | **10** | Reduced Inequalities |
| **2** | Zero Hunger | **11** | Sustainable Cities and Communities |
| **3** | Good Health and Well-being | **12** | Responsible Consumption and Production |
| **4** | Quality Education | **13** | Climate Action |
| **5** | Gender Equality | **14** | Life Below Water |
| **6** | Clean Water and Sanitation | **15** | Life on Land |
| **7** | Affordable and Clean Energy | **16** | Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions |
| **8** | Decent Work and Economic Growth | **17** | Partnerships for the Goals |
| **9** | Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure | | |

- Adopted by all UN member states on **25 September 2015** ("**Global Goals**"); in force from **1 January 2016**; deadline **2030**.
- The goals are **integrated** — action in one area affects others — balancing **social, economic and environmental** sustainability.
- The **5 Ps**: **People, Planet, Prosperity, Peace, Partnership**.
- Predecessor: the **8 Millennium Development Goals (MDGs)** from the **Millennium Summit, 2000**, with a **2015** deadline.

## Milestones of sustainable development

| Year | Event | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| **1972** | **Stockholm** — UN Conference on the Human Environment | Led to **UNEP**; same year the Club of Rome's **"Limits to Growth"** |
| **1987** | **Brundtland Commission** | Report **"Our Common Future"** — definition of sustainable development |
| **1992** | **Rio Earth Summit** | **Agenda 21** |
| **2002** | **Johannesburg** (Rio+10) | World Summit on Sustainable Development |
| **2012** | **Rio+20** | **"The Future We Want"**; launch of the **PAGE** green-economy partnership |
| **2015** | UN Summit, New York | **2030 Agenda** — 17 SDGs |

## India's monitoring

- **MoSPI** maintains the **National Indicator Framework (NIF)** for SDG monitoring; **NITI Aayog** coordinates the SDGs and publishes the **SDG India Index**.
- SDG India Index editions: **2018** (India score **57**), **2019** (60), **2020-21** (66), **2023-24** (71); the 2023-24 edition tracks **16 goals** on **113** indicators.

## Andhra Pradesh — sustainability angle

- **Harita AP**: green cover of **30%** (January 2026) to be raised to **37% by 2030** and **50% by 2047**.
- AP's commissioned renewable-energy capacity is about **14,833 MW** (NREDCAP, 31 August 2026); the state targets **160 GW** of green energy by **2047**.

## Don't confuse

- **SDG 14 Life Below Water** vs **SDG 15 Life on Land**; **SDG 12** consumption vs **SDG 13** climate.
- **Agenda 21** = Rio **1992**; **Agenda 2030** = SDGs, **2015**.

**TL;DR**
- 17 SDGs (7 = clean energy, 13 = climate, 14 = life below water, 16 = peace/justice, 17 = partnerships).
- Adopted 25 Sep 2015; in force 1 Jan 2016; 5 Ps; MDGs 8 goals (2000-2015).
- Stockholm 1972 (UNEP) → Brundtland 1987 → Rio 1992 (Agenda 21) → Johannesburg 2002 → Rio+20 2012 (Future We Want, PAGE).
- MoSPI NIF; SDG India Index scores 57 (2018) → 71 (2023-24).
- Harita AP: 30% → 37% (2030) → 50% (2047); AP RE ~14,833 MW; 160 GW by 2047.
keyPoints: SDG 1 No Poverty, 2 Zero Hunger, 3 Good Health, 4 Quality Education, 5 Gender Equality, 6 Clean Water and Sanitation.

SDG 13 Climate Action, 14 Life Below Water, 15 Life on Land, 16 Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions, 17 Partnerships for the Goals.

items.title: For Mains — Human & Sustainable Development
items.body:
A high-frequency **Paper-IV (Economy & Development)** theme (also usable in Paper-V environment answers): why growth must be judged by human-development and sustainability yardsticks, not GDP. Organise around these dimensions.

| Dimension | Content to deploy |
|---|---|
| **Concept** | Sen's capability approach; growth = means, development = end; intergenerational equity |
| **Measurement** | HDI (3 dims, geometric mean), IHDI/GDI/GII, MPI (H×A), PQLI, Green GDP, GNH |
| **India's standing** | HDR 2025 rank, inequality loss, MPI decline |
| **Sustainability** | Brundtland, SDGs, climate-growth trade-off, green economy |
| **Delivery / federalism** | SDG India Index as competitive + cooperative federalism tool |

**Data points & authorities to quote:** **HDR 2025** — India **130/193, HDI 0.685** (Medium), up from 134 (0.644); **~30.7% HDI loss to inequality** (IHDI ~0.475); **National MPI** headcount **24.85% (2015-16) → 14.96% (2019-21)**, ~13.5 crore escaped; **SDG India Index 2023-24**: India **71**, Kerala & Uttarakhand top (79), 32 Front Runners; **Brundtland (1987)**, **SDGs 17 goals/169 targets (2015)**; thinkers **Amartya Sen, Mahbub-ul-Haq, Morris D. Morris (PQLI)**; Bhutan's **GNH**; **Green GDP**.

**AP angle:** Andhra Pradesh is an **SDG Front Runner** that **topped SDG-7 (Affordable & Clean Energy)** on the strength of renewable capacity and electrification; its digitised welfare delivery supports MPI-indicator gains, making it a useful state case for 'localising the SDGs' and Viksit Bharat @2047.

**Use in answers:** (1) open with 'growth is a means, human development the end' (Sen); (2) tabulate HDI vs MPI vs SDG Index to show command of measures; (3) use India's rank-rise + MPI decline as evidence of progress, and the inequality loss as the caveat; (4) close on sustainability — development must not erode the base for future generations (Brundtland).
keyPoints: Frame: capability approach + measures (HDI/MPI/SDG Index) + India's standing + sustainability.
Quote HDR 2025 (India 130/193, HDI 0.685), ~30.7% inequality loss, MPI 24.85%→14.96%.
SDG India Index 2023-24: India 71, Kerala & Uttarakhand top (79); competitive+cooperative federalism.
Thinkers: Sen (capabilities), Mahbub-ul-Haq (HDI), Morris (PQLI); Brundtland defines sustainable development.
AP angle: SDG Front Runner, tops SDG-7 (clean energy); digitised welfare aids MPI gains.
